memories.content: Use the same term throughout the proposal for the same interaction concept or interface element.
Use abbreviations only for recurring terms of three or more words.
Present the full name and abbreviation together when using an abbreviation for the first time.
Prioritize the research role over diagnostic labels or deficits when referring to participants.
Reviewers from different subfields struggle to infer undefined abbreviations from context alone.
Use the term formative evaluation for studies seeking design modification evidence, and distinguish it from final efficacy judgments.
The user can have contribution labels such as principles, models, or guidelines approved only if they align with the abstraction level of the actual deliverables.
Design principles describe the relationship between conditions and outcomes rather than serving as instructions that merely replicate a single screen layout.
Specify field and user data sources and analysis procedures corresponding to all HCI research questions.
In preregistered studies, clarify the criteria for judging plan changes.
In preregistered studies, clarify the location for recording plan changes.
Use a justified minimum-to-maximum target range when confirmations can change, and tie the minimum and maximum to different workload and budget cases.
Specify the observation records, system logs, or interview tools used to collect each type of field and user data.
Specify whether each type of field and user data will be collected before, during, or after deployment.
Readers cannot assess a target range unless both bounds have a stated consequence for schedule, workload, or cost.
In field deployments, network and service instability exist as independent causes of task failure alongside design choices.
If a safety signal occurs in the field system, existing institutional safety procedures take precedence over the research schedule and data collection plan.
Reviewers judge answerability by tracing the path from each research question to its data sources and analysis procedures.
The user authoring this proposal tends to present implemented feature lists directly as design contributions.
Define what can still be completed at the minimum target instead of treating every number inside the range as operationally identical.
Use a bounded range to absorb expected confirmation changes without pretending that one early estimate is guaranteed.
Show how session count and facilitator time change at the minimum and maximum bounds.
Define the additional workload or deliverable enabled at the maximum target so the upper bound is not an arbitrary cushion.
A bounded range preserves uncertainty honestly but makes the final workload and budget less certain than one fixed target.

analysis.overview: The frames largely cover complementary proposal guidance. Their shared concern is calibrating claimed design contributions to actual abstraction, while the reference emphasizes terminology and participant framing and the compared frame emphasizes methodological traceability, preregistration, target ranges, field contingencies, and safety.

relations.reason: The reference provides the labeling rule and defines principles above single-layout instructions, while the compared frame identifies the authoring tendency that the rule addresses; all claims can jointly guide contribution framing.
relations.summary: Design-contribution labels should reflect the abstraction of actual deliverables rather than directly elevating implemented features into principles or similar contributions.

relations.reason: This is an independently useful terminology-consistency rule supplied only by the reference frame.
relations.summary: Use one consistent term for each interaction concept or interface element throughout the proposal.

relations.reason: This is a distinct abbreviation-eligibility rule supplied only by the reference frame.
relations.summary: Reserve abbreviations for recurring terms containing at least three words.

relations.reason: The reference supplies a first-use rule and its reviewer-comprehension rationale, which together express one underlying abbreviation-definition claim.
relations.summary: Introduce each abbreviation with its full name because cross-subfield reviewers cannot reliably infer undefined abbreviations from context.

relations.reason: This participant-framing policy appears only in the reference frame and is independent of its terminology mechanics.
relations.summary: Refer to participants by their research role rather than foregrounding diagnostic labels or deficits.

relations.reason: This study-purpose terminology rule appears only in the reference frame.
relations.summary: Use formative evaluation for studies seeking evidence to modify a design and distinguish that purpose from final efficacy judgment.

relations.reason: The compared memories divide one methodological traceability requirement into its data-source, collection-tool, timing, analysis, and reviewer-answerability components.
relations.summary: Make every HCI research question assessable through a traceable evidence path specifying data sources, collection instruments and timing, and analysis procedures.

relations.reason: The compared frame splits one plan-change documentation policy into decision criteria and recording location.
relations.summary: For preregistered studies, state both how plan changes will be judged and where they will be recorded.

relations.reason: The compared memories collectively state one bounded-range policy, operationalize both bounds, explain reviewer needs, and preserve the tradeoff that ranges reduce false precision while leaving workload and budget less certain.
relations.summary: When confirmations may change, use an honestly uncertain bounded target whose minimum and maximum have explicit, different consequences for feasible work, sessions, facilitator time, budget, and deliverables.

relations.reason: This field-deployment attribution consideration appears only in the compared frame.
relations.summary: Treat network and service instability as field-task failure causes independent of design choices.

relations.reason: This safety-governance priority appears only in the compared frame and is independent of other field-deployment guidance.
relations.summary: When a field-system safety signal occurs, institutional safety procedures take precedence over the research schedule and data collection plan.

reports.both: Both address avoiding inflated design-contribution claims by matching labels to deliverable abstraction rather than treating implemented features as principles.
reports.compared_only: The compared frame adds research-question traceability, preregistration-change documentation, operationally meaningful target ranges, field-failure attribution, and safety precedence.
reports.reference_only: The reference adds consistent terminology, disciplined abbreviation use, participant-first framing, and precise use of formative evaluation.
